findings: Exact diffs show the reviewed wake core and adapter algorithms/symbols unchanged; only include names and header guards differ. The private whole sweet_touch source differs from the hardware-observed persistent version only by two canonical header/bind includes and nawa_after_persistent() immediately after npa_persistent_window returned retained==1. The ordinary ncc branch and old retained cleanup logic are untouched.

The new nord2wifiwake boot argument must equal 1; default mode returns after parsing with no new mappings, native MMIO, result logging or AP-wake state mutation. Owner refusal checks software only: old persistent/global and outer latches, entered/retained/fatal/phase10/terminal2, no semaphore or SPI in flight, sole input owner and existing handles. It does not call ncc_ap_check, old npa/npc callbacks, PMIF or off-domain getter before wake.

Native raw address switch reuses SPM, infra, GALS, HOST, CFG and RGU handles with exact offsets. The reviewed adapter still gates first HOST1a0 read by six always-on AP checks, allows CFG only after ACK/clock/IRQ and awake proof, and allows the five cold RGU/HOST reads only after identity. No new map or DRAM/MPU/firmware/CPU-release path is introduced.

A distinct nawa_native one-shot object owns its AP wake reference. The source core latches reference before HOST1a0 write1; native write uses ordered ni_wr plus barrier. Sleep HOST1a0 write0 is the last backend callback; after ordered success, adapter marks asleep and the binding reads only in-memory result fields for logs. The old npa state and persistent lifetime are never modified by this binding.

Any uncertain post-reference failure retains the AP wake reference and takes a manual-reset panic without old cleanup. An initial nonzero HOST vote or clean prewrite proof failure has no wake write and reports diagnostic refusal while retaining phase10 common ownership. Reentry panics before further MMIO.
